children: GlobalFoundries finalized a $375 million CHIPS Act agreement with the U.S. government to expand domestic quantum manufacturing capabilities.

Under the five-year agreement, the semiconductor manufacturer will receive milestone-based research and development funding from the U.S. Department of Commerce to support quantum hardware developers transition from lab prototypes to commercial-scale manufacturing.
GlobalFoundries on Tuesday said that the funding is aimed at securing critical technologies necessary to build scalable quantum processing units in the U.S.
The news follows related announcements earlier Tuesday in which the Department of Commerce awarded $100 million each to D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing and Quantinuum.
As part of the agreements, the federal government took minority equity stakes in D-Wave and Rigetti, while Quantinuum selected GlobalFoundries as its primary manufacturing partner in the U.S.
